A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–I. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original surrogate-model evaluations, augmentation and refinement ablations, sensitivity analyses, and gigapixel-image and NeRF experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including the scientific-simulation, image-representation, and NeRF evaluations.

M1.justification: The DRR formulation, DRR-Net encoders and refiners, caching procedure, and VP augmentation remain unchanged. The redesigned Figure 1 illustrates the existing procedure rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Nyx, MPAS-Ocean, and Cloverleaf3D tasks, gigapixel reconstruction and super-resolution on the same two images, and novel-view synthesis on Lego and Drums.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain identical participants: K-Planes, FA-INR, and Explorable-INR for surrogates; the same augmentation and refinement variants; and the same Grid, MRGrid, TriPlane, NGP, SIREN, and NeRF comparisons in Appendix I.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, resolutions, model configurations, training budgets, preprocessing, sampling procedures, and metrics are unchanged in Section 4, Appendix B, and Appendix I. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The augmentation study, component ablations, positional-encoding and grid-resolution sensitivity studies, VP noise studies, and qualitative analyses are retained unchanged in Table 4 and Appendices C–H.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and FLOP/timing averaging procedures in Appendix B.3. No seed information, repeated-training-run counts, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 2–4 and 7–12 and the empirical figures are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports Nyx DRR-Net PSNR of 44.69 and inference time of 10.7 seconds in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–7, including residual refinement, multi-resolution unification, and VP interpolation, are unchanged. Figure 1 introduces no new formal reasoning or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about DRR, DRR-Net, VP augmentation, fidelity, and inference efficiency, including the up-to-27-fold speed claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of refinement, augmentation, dataset geometry, and failure cases remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning embedding structures, refiner architectures, and interpolation versus extrapolation.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, normalization, sampling, and timing details. The stated code link and configuration/data-parameter access instructions are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to earlier INR and surrogate methods are unchanged; reference pagination shifts without changing content.

P1.justification: Figure 1's caption adds the terminology 'feature grid' and removes references to the former lettered panels. Its internal labels are rewritten, while the main prose, appendix prose, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the horizontal architecture comparison and explicit preprocessing blocks with a throughput–expressiveness diagram and a two-stage DRR inset. Its narrower, taller layout causes subsequent reflow. Other figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The redesigned Figure 1 makes the existing two-stage workflow and throughput–expressiveness trade-off more explicit, but uses smaller, denser labels. This localized presentation trade-off leaves overall quality essentially unchanged; the methods, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical.
